newsitem.title: USA: Clinton optimistic on budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Clinton optimistic on budget talks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday he was encouraged about balanced budget negotiations with Congress and predicted an agreement would give a "new jolt" of confidence to the economy.
"The progress we've made so far is encouraging, and I'm hopeful that a bipartisan balanced budget agreement can be reached," Clinton said at the start of a brief White House news conference.
White House and congressional negotiators are trying to reach agreement on spending cuts that would bring the federal deficit to zero by 2002.
"If we passed a balanced budget, I think it would remove a lot of other lingering fears about inflation out there," Clinton said. "I think it would give a new jolt of confidence to the economy."

"There is no question that serious differences remain," he said, "but if each of us is willing to compromise our sense of the perfect, I know we can reach an agreement that advances the greater good."
